title: Exact scalar realization for all admissible condensed coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$, and let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$. Let $\Lambda$ be any of $A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, regarded as a condensed ring with the discrete topology for $A$ and the $\ell$-adic topology otherwise [sk-def-localizing-closure]. In particular the algebraic closure has the continuous-function condensed ring, without imposing that a section land in a finite subextension. Put $R=\Lambda(*)$. For any scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme], on its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. For an $R$-module $M$ let $\underline M$ be its constant module sheaf and set
$$C_T(M)=B_T\otimes_{\underline R}\underline M,$$
using the canonical constant-scalar map and ordinary module tensor [def-sfb-finite-constant-model-data, def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. Then $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and $C_T$ is additive and exact on all $R$-modules: every short exact scalar sequence gives a short exact sequence of $B_T$-module sheaves. These conclusions also hold after restriction to every localized site over an object $U$ of $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], with coefficient sheaf $B_T|_U$. For finite $A$ there is a canonical ring identification $B_T\cong\underline A$. For $R=\mathcal O_E$ there is a canonical ring identification
$$B_T\cong\varprojlim_{n\ge1}\underline{R/\pi_E^n},$$
and this actual completed coefficient sheaf is flat over $\underline R$, meaning that tensoring with it preserves all short exact sequences of $\underline R$-module sheaves. For $R=\mathbf Z_\ell$ the same assertion holds with $\pi_E=\ell$.

proof.text: Evaluation at the one-point profinite set identifies $R=\Lambda(*)=C(*,\Lambda)$ canonically with the underlying scalar ring: a continuous function on a point is determined by its value. For finite $A$, any ideal is generated by its finitely many elements, including the zero-ring case. For a field every nonzero ideal contains a unit and is the whole ring, so its ideals are generated by $0$ or $1$. Thus the three field cases are Noetherian, including the algebraic closure. For $\mathcal O_E$, the DVR theorem gives a principal ideal domain, hence a Noetherian ring by the cited PID theorem. Its specialization to the degree-one extension $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ gives the same conclusion for $\mathbf Z_\ell$. These are exactly all the scalar rings in the statement.

source.place: Paragraphs 2--3, scalar rings of the perfect local models; elementary finite-ring and field ideal arguments, and the cited DVR/PID results.

proof.text: The functor is additive for every coefficient ring in the statement. Constant sheafification sends the pointwise identity $(f+g)(m)=f(m)+g(m)$ to the same identity of sheaf morphisms. On a local pure tensor, $C_T(f+g)(b\otimes m)=b\otimes(f(m)+g(m))=C_T(f)(b\otimes m)+C_T(g)(b\otimes m)$ by the balancing construction. The same calculation sends the zero map to zero. Since pure tensors locally generate the sheaf tensor product, these are equalities of morphisms. Also $C_T(0)=0$.

source.place: Tag 093J (lemma-constant-exact); additivity from the constant and relative tensor constructions.

proof.text: For any short exact sequence $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ of $R$-modules, apply the exact constant-module-sheaf functor on the small site $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$. The cited theorem applies to every commutative scalar ring and every small site, so it gives $0\to\underline{M'}\to\underline M\to\underline{M''}\to0$. The small skeleton and ambient universe are precisely those already fixed for this pro-étale site; no finiteness of the modules is required. We use this constant sequence below before extending scalars.

source.place: Tag 093J (lemma-constant-exact): exactness of constants on any site.

proof.text: For finite discrete $A$, the cited coefficient-equivalence theorem identifies the actual pulled-back ring $B_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ with the constant ring sheaf $\underline A$, as rings. Use its canonical constant-ring identification, which carries each scalar $a$ to the constant section $a$. Extension along it is the tensor-unit identification: $b\otimes m\mapsto bm$, with inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$, locally on sections. The two composites are identities by the balancing relation. Hence $C_T(M)\cong\underline M$ naturally in every $A$-module $M$. Step 3 therefore proves exactness in this case as well as the required coefficient-ring identification.

source.place: Paragraphs 2--3, finite discrete coefficient specialization; finite constant coefficient comparison and tensor unit.

proof.text: For $R=\mathcal O_E$, apply the integral coefficient limit theorem to the scheme $T$. Its third clause gives the canonical ring isomorphism $B_T\cong\varprojlim_{n\ge1}\underline{R/\pi_E^n}$. This is the continuous, completed coefficient sheaf in the statement. Under each projection the canonical constant scalar $r$ maps to its residue class modulo $\pi_E^n$: both are induced by the scalar's constant continuous function followed by reduction. These equalities characterize the map to the inverse limit, so the isomorphism respects the canonical $\underline R$-algebra structures, not just the underlying rings. Specializing the same theorem to the degree-one extension $\mathbf Q_\ell/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation ring $\mathbf Z_\ell$ and uniformizer $\ell$, proves its asserted identification.

source.place: Steps 3--4: identification via representable profinite coefficients and their ring operations, not commutation of inverse image with arbitrary inverse limits.

proof.text: Use the completed-constant-sheaf theorem with the Noetherian ring $R$ from Step 1 and ideal $I=(\pi_E)$, or $(\ell)$ for $R=\mathbf Z_\ell$. Its flatness conclusion applies to $\varprojlim_{n\ge1}\underline{R/I^n}$ on every scheme, without a finite-generation condition on the sheaf modules being tensored. Step 5 identifies this algebra with $B_T$ over $\underline R$. Consequently tensoring with the actual $B_T$ preserves every short exact sequence of $\underline R$-module sheaves. Apply this to the short exact constant sequence from Step 3 to obtain exactness of $C_T$ on all scalar modules. This also proves the stronger sheaf-module flatness clause requested in the statement.

source.place: Tag 093M (lemma-completion-flat), with I generated by the uniformizer; Tag 093J for the constant sequence.

proof.text: For $R=\mathbf Q_\ell,E$, or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, consider an arbitrary scalar short exact sequence $0\to M'\xrightarrow{i}M\xrightarrow{q}M''\to0$. The vector-space projectivity theorem and its lifting definition give an $R$-linear section $s:M''\to M$ with $qs=1$. The isomorphism $M'\oplus M''\to M$ is $(x,y)\mapsto i(x)+s(y)$; its inverse sends $m$ to $(i^{-1}(m-sq(m)),q(m))$, where exactness makes the first component well-defined. Thus the sequence is split exact. Additivity from Step 2 preserves these biproduct identities and the splitting, so its image under $C_T$ is split exact and hence short exact. This uses the actual $B_T$ throughout. In particular no discreteness, completeness, finite-dimensionality, or finite-subextension condition on sections of the continuous algebraic-closure coefficient sheaf is used.

source.place: Tags 09FN (lemma-vector-space-is-free), 09FP (lemma-field-semi-simple); projective lifting as in algebra.tex Tag 05CF.

proof.text: Let $U\to T$ be any object of the small pro-étale site. The coefficient localization theorem identifies $U_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with $(T_{\mathrm{proét}})/U$ and identifies $B_T|_U$ with $p_U^*\Lambda$ for the same condensed ring $\Lambda$. This theorem allows arbitrary condensed rings, so applies also to the continuous-function algebraic-closure ring of the item. Under this equivalence of sites, a constant presheaf is still constant and coverings are the same, so its sheafification is the constant sheaf on the localized site. Repeat Steps 2--7 for the scheme $U$, transporting along that site and coefficient identification. Those steps assumed only that the base was a scheme, so all their hypotheses still hold. This proves additivity and scalar exactness, the finite and integral ring identifications, and full integral sheaf-module flatness on every localized site. The scalar ring $R$ and its Noetherian property in Step 1 are independent of the base.
